context_complement.quote: A disease name that premodifies, or is the complement of, a context or population noun (such as *cases*, *population*, *history*, *risk*, or *incidence*) is annotated **Modifier**.

modifier.quote: A textual string may refer to a disease name, but it may modify a noun phrase (or may not be a noun phrase itself). In such cases, annotate using the **Modifier** category.

specific.quote: - **Specific Disease**: Mentions that can be linked to one specific definition that does not include further categorization.

synonym.quote: Abbreviation definitions such as “Huntington disease” (“HD”) are separated into two annotated mentions (one for the long form, one for the abbreviation).

gene.quote: If a disease-denoting span (full name or abbreviation) occupies the leading premodifying position of a multi-token gene or protein name, meaning it is followed by a gene/protein head noun and optionally by a numeral or bracketed symbol, label only the disease-denoting tokens **Modifier**. Do not label them O, even though the whole designation reads as a proper name. Leave the head noun, numerals, and bracketed symbols outside the entity.

fixed_deficiency.quote: It is never excluded when it is part of a fixed disease name, such as “glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.”

duplicate.quote: For each sentence in the PubMed abstract and title, the locations of all disease mentions are marked, including duplicates within the same sentence.

span.quote: Use the smallest span necessary to include all tokens expressing the most specific form of the disease.

patient.quote: A mention whose head noun denotes a disease process or pathological category (for example, a process-suffix nominal such as “telangiectasis,” or a generic infection or inflammation term such as “infection”) is annotated **Specific Disease**, not Disease Class, when the document uses it as the patient's own diagnosis or presenting condition.

composite.quote: A textual string may refer to two or more separate disease mentions. Such mentions are annotated with the **Composite Mention** category.
